clue.text: Avoid drink, presumably after flipping work

indicators.note: after flipping says the letters just built are turned round end to end

parts.note: to avoid drink is, presumably, to sup nothing: SUP (drink) followed by O (nothing)

explanation.surface: Advice to stay off the booze, apparently after someone has lost their temper at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid drink' is read as 'sup O', drinking nothing, and 'presumably' admits the stretch; 'after flipping' turns SUPO round.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a piece of creative work.

clue.text: Combination of wine and port entertaining a group of players

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the wine holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: pinot is a grape and the wine made from it
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A drinks party mixing wine and port to amuse a band of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano trio is a chamber ensemble of piano, violin and cello.

clue.text: Smoother young man introducing a director

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the other letters are placed inside

parts.note: a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: A youth bringing in a film director for an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadiron is an old flatiron heated on a stove, used for pressing clothes smooth.

clue.text: Group of representatives name Democrat to replace Republican

indicators.note: to replace says one letter is swapped out for another in the word for name

parts.note: a good name is a reputation
R is the usual abbreviation for a US Republican
D is the usual abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: American party politics: a Democrat named in place of a Republican for a delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' puts D where R stood in REPUTATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputation is a body of people sent to speak or act on behalf of others, a delegation.

clue.text: At teen disco, much excitement … created by this 60s' hit?

indicators.note: excitement suggests agitation, so the letters of the preceding words are stirred up

explanation.surface: A teenage disco in a frenzy, all caused by one old pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tune itself: a 1968 hit by Sly and the Family Stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance to the Music was a 1968 single by the American band Sly and the Family Stone.

clue.text: Part of ploughman's lunch? Don't you believe it

definitions.meaning: a ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle, to which a cold meat pie might be added
a porky pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A pub menu item, and a warning that someone is spinning a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: a porky pie is a lie, so the second definition says 'that's a fib'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a cold pastry filled with pork and, in rhyming slang, a falsehood.

clue.text: To trap crooked drug dealer, they'd fixed bug

indicators.note: to trap means to hold something caught inside, so one set of letters surrounds the other
fixed means rigged, so the letters of they'd are rearranged
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of drug dealer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police planting a listening device to catch a corrupt narcotics dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' gives THEDY, split round READEDLURG ('crooked' drug dealer) by 'To trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dreaded lurgy is a jokey British name for any contagious illness, a bug going round.

clue.text: Traveller who'll remove clothes except for hat?

indicators.note: except for hat means without its top, the first letter, removed

parts.note: a stripper is someone who takes their clothes off

explanation.surface: A traveller who'll undress completely apart from their headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hat' of a down word is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A day tripper is a sightseer or holidaymaker on a short excursion, so a traveller.

clue.text: Different article with gold edges

indicators.note: edges means the word for gold forms the borders on either side

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A distinctive item trimmed with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means unlike or distinct from the one already mentioned.

clue.text: Horticulturist, say, circulating round forest close to Leicester

indicators.note: round tells us those letters are placed around the forest
circulating suggests going round, so the abbreviation for say is turned back to front

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
the Forest of Arden is the woodland of Shakespeare's As You Like It

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of Leicester

explanation.surface: A plant expert doing a tour of a woodland near the city of Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' reverses the abbreviation for 'say' into GE. Arden is the English forest in Warwickshire where Shakespeare set As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends plants and gardens is a horticulturist, whether amateur or professional.

clue.text: Priest quiet when brought before a prophet

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A silent cleric ushered in to meet a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was the Old Testament prophet who succeeded Elijah.

clue.text: Unrefined-sounding series of lectures

indicators.note: sounding says we want a word that is pronounced like the word for unrefined

parts.note: unrefined means coarse, rough or crude

explanation.surface: A lecture series that comes across as rather crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A university course is a planned set of classes or lectures on one subject.

clue.text: Very good recipe: I doubled the chilli sauce

indicators.note: doubled says the little string built so far is written out twice

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A cook boasting about a recipe that calls for twice the hot sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Peri-peri is a hot sauce made from African bird's-eye chillies, popular in Portuguese cooking.

clue.text: Don Carlos, say, smuggled drug into Greece and Austria

indicators.note: into says the smuggled drug goes inside the letters for Greece

parts.note: GR is the international vehicle code for Greece
to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran
dope is a slang word for a drug
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A tale of a man named Don Carlos running narcotics across European borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Carlos is not a smuggler but Verdi's five-act opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Don Carlos is an example of the large-scale, serious, fully sung style of nineteenth-century opera.

clue.text: Book about the present era?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
AD, anno Domini, labels years of the present era

explanation.surface: Asking for a book about modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a good read is a book worth reading, so the word stands for a book.

clue.text: Surprise! Hampton Court employees wear brimless hats

indicators.note: wear says the hats go on and around the employees
brimless means the hats lose their outer letters

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace has a famous hedge maze, so its staff could be maze men

explanation.surface: A surprise sight: palace staff in caps with no brims.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court is a royal palace near London famous for its hedge maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is the feeling of great surprise or wonder.

clue.text: Hooligan taking part in school outing

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A troublemaker joins a class trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is an uncouth, aggressive young man, a yob or hooligan.

clue.text: Murdoch's novel clanger

definitions.meaning: Iris Murdoch wrote a 1958 novel of this name about a religious community
a clanger here is literally something that clangs, a ringing object

explanation.surface: A literary blunder in a book by Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clanger' looks like a British word for a gaffe; it means something that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of an Iris Murdoch novel is also the name of a ringing instrument that clangs.

clue.text: Shark movie opens after actor and leading lady take charge

indicators.note: after places the movie's opening letter behind the word for actor

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: opens means the first letter of movie

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the realm's leading lady
to head something is to take charge of it

explanation.surface: A film premiere where the star and his co-star seize control of a shark picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a species of shark with a flattened, hammer-shaped head.

clue.text: Fixed attitude of nurses initially estimating temperature

parts.note: to nurse is to look after, mind

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Nurses stuck in their ways when it comes to taking temperatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is an established way of thinking, a settled outlook.

clue.text: Society in a stew where there's political unrest?

indicators.note: in says the society letter is placed inside the stew

parts.note: a Lancashire hotpot is a meat and potato stew

explanation.surface: A society all worked up, in a place seething with political trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotpot is a British stew of meat topped with sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a place of conflict or danger, where trouble may flare up.

clue.text: Mean lads disturbed Yorkshire resident

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty youths causing trouble for someone living in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are a region of upland valleys in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman is a native or inhabitant of the dales, especially of Yorkshire.

clue.text: A large weapon creates it?

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A big gun causes panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, which the sight of a big weapon would provoke.

clue.text: Refuse conveyance for the wounded

definitions.meaning: refuse here is rubbish, scattered waste
a stretcher or covered couch for carrying the sick or injured

explanation.surface: Rubbish and a stretcher for casualties set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both discarded rubbish and a frame on which an injured person is carried.

clue.text: Cast half-rejected some weird parts

indicators.note: half-rejected says the back half of cast is thrown away, keeping its first two letters
weird signals that the letters of some are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cast half turned down some strange roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-rejected' keeps only the front half of the four-letter word; 'weird' rearranges SOME into EOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small, often distinctive role in a film or play, typically played by a well-known actor.

clue.text: Son caught, given beating

parts.note: trapped means caught

explanation.surface: A boy is nabbed and then thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap someone is to beat them with a leather belt, so this is a past-tense idiom for a thrashing.

clue.text: I'm right to be in work? Absolutely

parts.note: I'm gives its letters as written

indicators.note: to be in says the word for right sits inside the word for work

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
licit means lawful, right

explanation.surface: Someone checking that taking a job is legitimate, and being told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust someone implicitly is to trust them completely and without question.

clue.text: Worthless stuff by independent film-maker

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods, junk

explanation.surface: An indie director whose output is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was the French director and comic actor behind Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.
